11. Products and Tenants

Four layers decide how a surface looks, each narrower than the last.

LayerWhoWhat it sets
SystemInstrumentStructure: type, shape, depth, space, motion, the neutral case, the status colors, hazard tape, the brace
OrganizationNCodeThe three anchors; --nc-brand is NCode Blue
ProductNCode Identity, NCode BuffersA mark of the mark's construction, a name, a descriptor and its cards. No color of its own
TenantA customer of NCode IdentityTwo colors, the theme, a logo and a display name, at run time

What a Product Owns

A product owns its mark, {id} for NCode Identity, its name and what it says about itself. It does not own a color: every NCode product is NCode Blue on NCode's own surfaces, so the family reads as one.

What a Tenant May Change

A tenant changes five things, the fields of NCode Identity's BrandingConfig: its name, its logo, its primary color, its secondary color and the theme.

  • primaryColor colors what you press. It becomes --nc-brand. Keys, links, the focus ring, selection and lit lamps derive from it.
  • secondaryColor colors what you are shown. It becomes --nc-brand-secondary. Screens, the display, the lit boundary plate and the tenant's scope braces derive from it. It follows the primary until a tenant sets it.
  • mode pins the theme with data-theme. Without it the page follows the system setting.
  • logoUrl fills the nameplate of the tenant's card.

A tenant cannot change the typefaces, the shapes, the neutral, the status colors, hazard tape or the brace. NCode's own marks go one color, the text color, under a tenant's colors: set data-brand="tenant" on the root, and they never take the tenant's hue.

One part of a page can run under other inputs: mark an element data-brand-scope and set --nc-brand on it, as a branding preview does. Inside it the secondary follows that element's own primary until it sets one.

How the Colors Are Derived

tokens/tokens.css derives everything the two inputs touch in CSS, with relative colors and color-mix(), and is calibrated on the logo kit: NCode Blue yields exactly NCode Navy for screens and exactly NCode Blue Light for the dark theme. Its rules hold these guarantees for the colors a tenant is likely to choose:

  • The label of a primary key is white or black, by the color's lightness, and a touched key's face moves away from its label, so hover and pressed keep their contrast.
  • The brand as text, as a line and as the focus ring is darkened to OKLCH lightness 0.48 at most in the light theme, and lifted to 0.72 in the dark theme.
  • The outline of a primary key is never lighter than OKLCH lightness 0.55, so the key reaches 3 to 1 against a light plate by its edge, whatever its face.
  • Every color on a screen is set to a fixed lightness, so a screen passes for any hue.

CSS cannot search, so a rule cannot raise a color that falls short. tokens/derive.mjs derives the same colors in JavaScript, then moves any color whose pairing is below its floor, in steps of OKLCH lightness, until it reaches it, and names what it moved in adjusted.

In a sweep of the sRGB cube, 729 colors in nine steps a channel, the rules of tokens.css hold every pairing for 698 of them. For the other 31, tokens/derive.mjs moves the colors below their floor (on-primary, primary-shade, primary-text, screen-lit) and holds every pairing for all 729, with 0 below the floor. For NCode Blue and the ten proof and stress colors it moves nothing, so it gives what tokens.css gives.

So a surface with one brand, such as NCode's documentation, takes the CSS derivation; an application that accepts any tenant's color, such as NCode Identity, sets the derived colors from tokens/derive.mjs, and a tenant can be told when a color was corrected. tokens/derive.vectors.json pins its results for a fixed list of inputs, NCode Blue, the proof and stress colors and the hard cases, so a consumer's tests can assert the same numbers this repository's do.

The Limit

The face of a primary key lighter than about OKLCH lightness 0.75 is faint on a light plate: yellow #FACC15 is 1.3 to 1 on the page and 1.4 to 1 on a plate. Its edge, its lip and its label still mark it, and no guard changes it, because the face is the tenant's own color. Whether a product accepts such a color as it is, warns the tenant or darkens it is the product's decision.
